negative_reviews.author: Hannah Allport (Raine)
negative_reviews.text: Went here for lunch with my friend and the wait time was incredibly long. We waited around 30 minutes for maki rolls and then, as a vegan, I was served a salmon roll and the server just left before I could say anything which was really frustrating. Then we waited even longer for the correct dish to be brought once the server came back. The food was really delicious once we got it but then we waited around 20 minutes waiting for the bill as well as being ignored multiple times. In the time, my friend was able to go to the nearby subway and back with cookies and i still hadn't been handed the bill. It was quite infuriating how a table next to us was offered a discount for a small error with a drinks order whilst the mixup with mine was treated with a brief sorry. Definitely put a damper on our day out. 😕

negative_reviews.author: Enn Xin
negative_reviews.text: Me and my bf went there to eat then they opened, the food wasn’t that great for the price we paid, a lot of the menu was unavailable, the waiter took our order for dessert and came back after a few minutes telling us it’s unavailable, we ended up having to order something else that was available. In the end we waited more than 30 minutes for 3 pieces of store bought mochi drizzled in chocolate (for £7) which you could find in Lidl, paying half the price. Haven’t been there since.

negative_reviews.author: Fatuuu ms
negative_reviews.text: Bro, I just wanted a fork to eat my noodles, and they walked away💀

negative_reviews.author: Chi Kin Fong
negative_reviews.text:
First visit but we both suffered tummy pain and got a lot of bloating at late night till now. The two bowls of ramen were not served hot enough in temperatures. The prawn tempura inside the sushi were not crispy (it would be oil temperature was too low or the batter was mixed too much)

Very disappointing on the food and not happy but service was fine...

issues: Covers fell by 39 (2%) week on week and spend per head fell by £0.48 (2.34%).
Sales were down £1,742.77 (4.22%) week on week and £529.98 (1.32%) below target.
Google reviews: 59 five star, 4 four star, two 2 star and two 1 star.
The 2 star reviews cited a long wait for food and the bill, and a backdated review about many menu items being unavailable.
The 1 star reviews cited a server walking away when a guest needed a fork, and a stomach ache after the visit with broth not hot enough and prawn tempura not crispy.
No audit was done this week.
Areas for improvement: cut labour whenever possible, and add extra staff on Saturdays to improve speed of service.

Southampton Crossings' property manager is interested in a frozen vending pilot for a 527 student residence, asked for a brochure and photos, and flagged a possible exclusivity restriction with its current vending supplier; the proposed 07/10 visit was not evidenced.
Southampton Crossings also discussed a separate one day resident stand, proposed for 19/10 with a 4pm to 6pm session; Unite Students Southampton forwarded the enquiry internally without committing.
Two delivery orders had missing items (tofu and belly).
One of the Saturday negative reviews also cited language issues, and Kaitlin Docherty noted that a complaint review had not yet been answered.
Saturdays are busy all day with a service gap between 3pm and 6pm, so fresh staff must start at 2pm, 3pm or 4pm to cover breaks rather than the same six people working the whole day.

Region: Ziang Lin introduced a mandatory seating upsell at all sites from 13/10: staff place the drinks menu from the marketing stand in the middle of the table and immediately offer edamame, and kitchens boil a large batch of edamame in advance so it can be blanched for five seconds when ordered.
Region: Kaitlin Docherty will send daily delivery performance (red, amber, green) to the group chats every day between 10:30 and 12:00 from 14/10.
